plan.planning_summary: Refining route_03 (SiO2/Al2O3 multi-cavity UV bandpass) based on iteration feedback. Three complementary routes test: (1) locked intermediate cavity with constrained Bragg mirrors per directive, (2) expanded Bragg period count with same cavity lock, (3) alternative HfO2/SiO2 material pair with identical topology. All routes maintain 25-29 layer counts within manufacturing constraint, preserve fused silica substrate, and optimize thicknesses while locking stabilized cavity segments identified in iteration_14.

routes.title: Locked cavity with full Bragg mirror optimization (25-layer SiO2/Al2O3)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Locking the intermediate cavity layers (13-17) to stabilized values from iteration_14 while allowing full optimization of outer Bragg mirrors will improve target score by reducing destructive interference triggers in the passband while maintaining rejection band degrees of freedom.
routes.design_principle: Periodic Bragg mirrors sandwich a fixed defect cavity. Outer layers control stopband edges; inner cavity controls passband resonance. Constraining cavity thickness prevents optimizer from destabilizing the transmission peak.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [SiO2/Al2O3]_12 | SiO2(70nm)/Al2O3(51nm)/SiO2(61nm)/Al2O3(47nm)/SiO2(61nm) | [Al2O3/SiO2]_6 | Fused Silica. Total 25 finite coating layers.
manufacturing_considerations: layers 13-17 fixed to iteration_14 best candidate values
outer layers bounded ±20% from quarter-wave at 267.5nm
theory_basis: Transfer Matrix Method for coherent thin-film interference
Bragg mirror stopband theory with defect cavity resonance
known_risks: fixed cavity may limit achievable passband width
outer mirrors may not compensate for cavity imperfections
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 25-layer SiO2/Al2O3 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layers 0-12 alternate SiO2/Al2O3 starting with SiO2. Layers 13-17 are fixed at thicknesses [70.0, 51.0, 61.0, 47.0, 61.0] nm with materials [SiO2, Al2O3, SiO2, Al2O3, SiO2]. Layers 18-24 alternate Al2O3/SiO2 ending with SiO2. Optimize thicknesses of layers 0-12 and 18-24 with bounds ±20% from quarter-wave optical thickness at 267.5nm center wavelength. Score candidates by mean transmittance in 255-280nm (maximize), 300-700nm (minimize), and 700-1100nm (minimize). Use coherent TMM solver across 255-1100nm spectrum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Implements feedback directive to lock stabilized cavity layers 13-17 from iteration_14 while permitting full optimization of Bragg mirrors to improve target score without destabilizing passband resonance.

routes.title: Expanded Bragg periods with locked cavity (29-layer SiO2/Al2O3)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Increasing Bragg mirror period count from 12+6 to 14+8 periods while maintaining the locked cavity will improve visible/NIR rejection without degrading UV passband, as additional mirror periods increase stopband depth.
routes.design_principle: More Bragg periods increase reflectivity in stopbands. The fixed cavity preserves passband characteristics while outer mirrors provide deeper rejection.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [SiO2/Al2O3]_14 | SiO2(70nm)/Al2O3(51nm)/SiO2(61nm)/Al2O3(47nm)/SiO2(61nm) | [Al2O3/SiO2]_8 | Fused Silica. Total 29 finite coating layers.
manufacturing_considerations: layers 14-18 fixed to iteration_14 cavity values
outer layers bounded ±20% from quarter-wave at 267.5nm
theory_basis: Bragg mirror stopband depth scales with period count
Transfer Matrix Method for multilayer interference
expected_advantages: maintained passband stability from locked cavity
known_risks: increased total thickness may introduce stress
may not improve if rejection already saturated
routes.execution_request_english: Optimize a 29-layer SiO2/Al2O3 dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Layers 0-13 alternate SiO2/Al2O3 starting with SiO2. Layers 14-18 are fixed at thicknesses [70.0, 51.0, 61.0, 47.0, 61.0] nm with materials [SiO2, Al2O3, SiO2, Al2O3, SiO2]. Layers 19-28 alternate Al2O3/SiO2 ending with SiO2. Optimize thicknesses of layers 0-13 and 19-28 with bounds ±20% from quarter-wave optical thickness at 267.5nm center wavelength. Score candidates by mean transmittance in 255-280nm (maximize), 300-700nm (minimize), and 700-1100nm (minimize). Use coherent TMM solver across 255-1100nm spectrum. Total finite layers = 29. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests whether increased Bragg period count (29 vs 25 layers) improves rejection bands while maintaining the locked cavity principle from iteration_14 feedback.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 material pair with locked cavity (25-layer)
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Replacing Al2O3 with HfO2 as the high-index material will improve UV transparency and refractive index contrast, leading to better passband transmission and stopband rejection with the same locked cavity topology.
routes.design_principle: HfO2 has higher refractive index (~2.19) than Al2O3 (~1.75) in UV range, providing stronger index contrast for Bragg mirrors while maintaining UV transparency per evidence on HfO2/SiO2 UV filters.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | [SiO2/HfO2]_12 | SiO2(70nm)/HfO2(51nm)/SiO2(61nm)/HfO2(47nm)/SiO2(61nm) | [HfO2/SiO2]_6 | Fused Silica. Total 25 finite coating layers.
manufacturing_considerations: layers 13-17 fixed to scaled cavity values
HfO2 requires ion-assisted deposition for density per evidence
theory_basis: Higher index contrast improves Bragg mirror reflectivity
HfO2 transparency in UV range per literature
expected_advantages: stronger stopband rejection from higher index contrast
material system validated for UV filters in evidence
known_risks: HfO2 may exhibit inhomogeneity per evidence
different optical constants require thickness rescaling
absorption edge may encroach on 255nm passband

Layers 13-17 are fixed at thicknesses [70.0, 51.0, 61.0, 47.0, 61.0] nm with materials [SiO2, HfO2, SiO2, HfO2, SiO2]. Layers 18-24 alternate HfO2/SiO2 ending with SiO2. Optimize thicknesses of layers 0-12 and 18-24 with bounds ±20% from quarter-wave optical thickness at 267.5nm center wavelength using HfO2 refractive index. Score candidates by mean transmittance in 255-280nm (maximize), 300-700nm (minimize), and 700-1100nm (minimize). Use coherent TMM solver across 255-1100nm spectrum. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 255-280 nm, 300-700 nm, 700-1100 nm. soft objectives: high transmittance in 255–280 nm; low transmittance in 300–700 nm; low transmittance in 700–1100 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: transmittance in 300–700 nm; transmittance in 700–1100 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layers ≤ 30; no metal layers; conventional depositable inorganic dielectric materials only.
routes.revision_reason: Tests alternative material pair (HfO2/SiO2 vs SiO2/Al2O3) while maintaining the locked cavity topology from iteration_14 to isolate material system effects on performance.
